props.gloss_en: broken above the knee joint, the majority of the flesh intact: both [animal and limb] are permitted
Rav: [above the knee] and if not [the majority of the flesh is not intact], both are forbidden
broken below the knee joint, the majority of the flesh intact: both are permitted
[below the knee] if not: the limb is forbidden and the animal permitted
Shmuel: whether above or below, if not [intact]: the limb is forbidden and the animal permitted -- so above the knee too
Rav Nachman, as first phrased: people will say 'a limb of it lies on the dunghill and it is permitted?'
Rav Nachman, as he meant it: people will say 'a limb from which it lives lies on the dunghill and it is permitted?'
the halakha follows Rav [on the break above the knee]
again they sent: [the halakha follows] Shmuel
and the limb itself imparts impurity by carrying

No: if the slaughter of a tereifa purifies it and the limb hanging from it -- a thing of its own body -- shall it purify the fetus, a thing not of its body? (conceding that slaughter purifies the hanging limb)
the mishna: [hanging limb and flesh,] the animal was slaughtered -- they were rendered susceptible by its blood, the words of R' Meir; R' Shimon says: they were not
R' Zeira: and so Aryokh interpreted it in Babylonia
who is Aryokh? Shmuel
Shmuel retracted [his view] in favour of Rav's
the baraita: a bone broke and protruded -- if skin and flesh cover its majority, it is permitted
the baraita: if not, it is forbidden
how much is its majority? R' Yochanan: most of its thickness
and some say [R' Yochanan said]: most of its circumference
Rav Pappa: therefore we require most of its thickness
Rav Pappa: and we require most of its circumference
R' Yochanan (via Ulla): skin is like flesh
R' Yochanan (via Ulla, in the איכא דאמרי version): skin combines with flesh
a fledgling in R' Yitzchak's house, where skin combined with flesh, came before R' Yochanan and he declared it fit
Rav Nachman: a fledgling, which is soft, is different
soft sinews [covering the break] came before Rabba; Rabba: what is there to be concerned about with them? -- permitted
R' Yochanan: sinews destined to harden -- one may be registered on them for the pesach [they count as flesh]
Rabba: and furthermore, the Torah spared the money of Israel
R' Shimon ben Lakish [disagrees: sinews destined to harden do not count] -- the text only names him
Rabba was silent
Rava: the halakha follows R' Shimon ben Lakish [against R' Yochanan] in these three
here it is different: R' Yochanan retracted in favour of R' Shimon ben Lakish
R' Yochanan to R' Shimon ben Lakish: do not provoke me -- I teach it as the view of a lone [tanna]
a bone broke and protruded and a chip was removed from it; it came before Abaye, who held it over three festivals
Rav Adda bar Mattana: go before Rava son of Rav Yosef bar Chama, whose knife is sharp
Rava: since we learned 'the bone broke and protruded', what is it to me whether [the chip] fell off or is there? -- [it is like any protruding bone: permitted]
Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua: 'decayed' is whatever the doctor scrapes away
(what the תא שמע at 77a.9 would show, if it held) a covering that is not intact flesh can still count -- for skin is like flesh
Rav Ashi: [flesh] cut away like a ring -- we resolved it [as fit, since the flesh can be made to heal]
Rav: I asked this of the Sages and the doctors, and they said: one scores it with a bone and it heals
but iron inflames it
Rav Pappa: and that is provided the bone holds its own [flesh]
